transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM); Jordan (CTO), Priya (Head of Security), Samir (DevOps), Nina (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Customer needs: healthcare data, sensitive PII/PHI, must meet SOC2/ISO and data residency.
- Key asks: SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit logs to SIEM, encryption (BYOK), VPC/private deployment options and retention policies.
- Next: send security artifact pack, schedule PoC deep dive, confirm timelines.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we appreciate your time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, with Maya our solutions engineer and Diego from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jordan: Good thanks, short intro from our side — I'm Jordan, CTO at Solstice. Priya is our head of security, Samir runs infra, Nina on product.
[00:20] Priya: Hi all. We're primarily here to understand the security posture for Redwood's hosted offering versus dedicated or private, what controls we can validate, and how we'd do a PoC safely with PHI in the loop.
[00:31] Maya: Great, that's the right set of questions. We'll walk through SOC2/ISO posture, SSO and provisioning, RBAC, audit logs and SIEM integration, and encryption/KMS options, and then talk about deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, private — and tradeoffs.
[00:43] Samir: Quick note — we're leaning toward hosted if we can get tenant isolation, BYOK, and logs shipped to our Splunk. If not, we'll consider dedicated or private. Cost is a factor but compliance is #1.
[00:58] Alex: Understood. Priya, do you have a list of must-have controls or certs? SOC2? ISO? FedRAMP?
[01:06] Priya: SOC2 Type II is required, ISO 27001 would be preferred. FedRAMP is not required for now but we may revisit. We also need SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning, RBAC down to team and token level, immutable audit logs, and the ability to bring our own key or use HSM-backed KMS. Also data residency — all PHI must stay in the US east region.
[01:27] Maya: Cool. On the certs, Redwood's hosted control plane is SOC2 Type II and we have an ISO certificate — we'll share those artifacts. For KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM integration on private deployments; for hosted we also offer a customer-managed key option with limited support depending on contract.
[01:43] Jordan: When you say "hosted" — is that multi-tenant? How do you isolate our data from other tenants?
[01:50] Maya: Yes hosted is multi-tenant logically partitioned. We do strict tenant isolation at the application and storage layer, encrypt at rest per-tenant, and we have network controls. For higher isolation we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) which gives isolated GPU pools and stronger network separation. For the strictest control, Private provides a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[02:09] Priya: Can you explain logs — what do you capture, retention, and can we stream to Splunk/Datadog?
[02:16] Maya: We capture request metadata, authentication events, model invocation traces (token counts, model id, latency), and admin actions. Audit logs are immutable and we can stream to Splunk via a connector or to an S3 bucket which you can ingest. Retention is configurable per contract — default 90 days for hosted, longer for enterprise add-ons.
[02:36] Samir: Is there a guaranteed SLA around log delivery?
[02:39] Diego: We can include delivery SLAs as part of Dedicated/Private agreements; hosted has best-effort with standard retention but enterprise add-on can guarantee delivery windows and retention.
[02:48] Jordan: Encryption at rest — is it AES-256? Who manages keys?
[02:52] Maya: AES-256 for disk encryption. By default Redwood manages keys, but we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations. For Private deployments you can bring your own HSM and we do BYOK with key rotation APIs.
[03:05] Priya: How about encryption in transit? TLS 1.2/1.3?
[03:08] Maya: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 enforced for all data in transit, mutual TLS available for private endpoints.
[03:15] Priya: SSO — you support SAML and OIDC? SCIM for provisioning?
[03:19] Maya: Yes, SAML 2.0 and OIDC supported, SCIM 2.0 for provisioning and deprovisioning. We also support SCIM user and group sync to keep RBAC consistent.
[03:29] Samir: RBAC granularity — can we scope keys to projects/environments and audit token usage by user?
[03:34] Maya: Yes tokens are scoped, and our RBAC supports role and resource level permissions. We have token-level attribution in audit logs so you can see which user or service used which token. Some of the names in the transcript may be a little off — the auto-transcript sometimes labels internal actions oddly.
[03:47] Jordan: Integration with our SIEM — do you have exporters or do we pull logs from S3?
[03:52] Maya: Both — we can push directly to Splunk/Datadog via connectors or you can pull from a secure S3 with cross-account access. For Dedicated/Private we also support syslog endpoints.
[04:02] Priya: What about data retention policy? We need N days for logs and deletion guarantees for model inputs/outputs.
[04:09] Maya: For hosted, default retention for raw inputs is 30 days, metadata 90 days; we offer configurable retention and strict deletion policies for enterprise customers. For Private we can meet whatever retention you need since it's customer-managed. We'll include a whitepaper with the retention SLA matrix.
[04:25] Nina: If we run a PoC and send PHI, what's the safe pattern? Tokenization? Redaction?
[04:31] Maya: We recommend either: a) mask or tokenize PHI before sending to hosted endpoints; b) use Dedicated with private network and customer-managed keys; or c) run the PoC in Private where data never leaves your VPC. For initial testing we often do a synthetic data set or redacted records.
[04:49] Priya: Are there audit reports we can use for our vendor risk assessment?
[04:53] Alex: Yes SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificate, vulnerability scanning reports, and a security whitepaper. We'll attach those to the follow-up.
[05:01] Jordan: Any third-party pen tests?
[05:04] Maya: We do annual third-party pen tests and internal red teams; summary reports are available under NDA.
[05:10] Samir: Networking — can you support private endpoints in our VPC?
[05:14] Maya: For Private we provision a control plane in your VPC. For Dedicated we have VPC peering options and private endpoints. Hosted supports VPC egress controls and allow-listing IPs for dedicated customers.
[05:25] Priya: Who has access to plaintext model inputs/outputs? Engineers? Support?
[05:29] Diego: Access is limited via RBAC and requires approval workflows. Support access to customer data is audited and must be enabled per-case, with just-in-time elevation and recorded in audit logs.
[05:41] Priya: Can you confirm data residency options — region locking?
[05:45] Maya: Yes, we support region locking so data stays in a chosen cloud region (US East, US West, EU). For Private it's entirely under your control.
[05:53] Jordan: If we go hosted with BYOK, do we lose the ability to rotate keys on our schedule?
[05:58] Maya: We offer an API for key rotation; with BYOK you control rotation cadence, but for some hosted setups rotation requires a short maintenance window. We'll document the exact steps.
[06:09] Samir: What about secrets management for API keys?
[06:12] Maya: We recommend using vaults (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault). We support integration patterns for secret retrieval at runtime and short-lived tokens for job-level access.
[06:21] Nina: Compliance team asked about data deletion proofs — can you provide attestations that data was deleted?
[06:26] Alex: We can provide deletion logs and time-stamped audit entries for deletion operations; for Private deployments you can run your own verification. We'll include examples in the artifact pack.
[06:36] Priya: For SOC2 — is it Type II and what's the coverage period?
[06:40] Alex: It's SOC2 Type II covering the last 12 months; we'll share the report and a summary of in-scope controls.
[06:47] Jordan: Any concerns around model outputs containing sensitive data? Are there guardrails?
[06:51] Maya: We have content filters and policy hooks, plus the ability to run post-processing to redact or block PHI outputs. Also we provide deterministic logging hooks to track which prompt produced what output.
[07:05] Jordan: Ok great. If we move to a PoC, what's the typical timeline?
[07:09] Maya: Usually 2-4 weeks for a basic PoC (connect SSO, set up keys, run sample workload). Deeper performance benchmarking can take longer. We'll scope that in the PoC runbook.
[07:18] Samir: For performance — if we need lower latency, does hosting in our region help?
[07:23] Maya: Yes latency drops if we host in the same region; Dedicated also helps since you get reserved GPUs and predictable latency.
[07:29] Priya: Any encryption certifications for HSM? FIPS 140-2?
[07:33] Maya: Our HSM integrations cover FIPS 140-2 level for customer-managed HSMs; we'll include details in the whitepaper.
[07:41] Jordan: Do you support VPC service endpoints and PrivateLink?
[07:44] Maya: We support PrivateLink and VPC endpoints for certain cloud providers on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has public endpoints but can be fronted with private connectivity in enterprise setups.
[07:55] Priya: For RBAC — can we map our Okta groups to Redwood roles?
[07:59] Maya: Yes via SCIM and SAML group assertions; you can map Okta groups to roles and also enforce attribute-based access in some cases.
[08:08] Nina: Are there any default admin accounts we should be aware of?
[08:12] Diego: No persistent backdoor accounts; we run admin accounts under control plane with strict logging. Any support access is logged and auditable.
[08:21] Jordan: Let's talk about the PoC data path — we need to ensure nothing lands in logs that could break compliance.
[08:27] Maya: For PoC we can set a retention policy to minimal, configure redaction, and route logs to your S3 for immediate ingestion and deletion.
[08:36] Priya: About pricing impact: if we enable BYOK and longer retention, will that affect cost materially?
[08:42] Alex: Yes some add-ons (BYOK, extended retention, dedicated GPU pools) have line-item costs. We'll include estimated pricing in the follow-up.
[08:52] Samir: For the PoC, we'll need a runbook and a checklist of required IAM roles and network changes.
[08:58] Maya: We'll produce a PoC runbook and a minimal network/IAM checklist.
[09:05] Jordan: Any references in healthcare you can share?
[09:09] Alex: We have anonymized case studies and reference customers in the space; we'll include contact details where allowed.
[09:15] Priya: One more question — do you retain model weights or fine-tuning artifacts? If we fine-tune on our data, who owns the artifacts?
[09:25] Maya: If you fine-tune in-hosted, artifacts can be stored under your tenant; contract defines ownership. For Private, artifacts never leave your infra. We'll point to the policy in the security doc.
[09:37] Nina: Ok, next steps?
[09:40] Alex: We'll send the artifact pack with SOC2, ISO, pen test summary, and the PoC runbook. Maya will reach out to schedule the technical kick-off. Priya and Samir, if you can share the list of required controls and network diagram that would help.
[09:54] Priya: We'll do that.
[09:56] Jordan: Anything else?
[09:58] Diego: Just to reiterate — we'll include a sample contract clause for BYOK and data residency.
[10:04] Samir: Good, thanks.
[10:06] Alex: Thanks everyone — talk soon.

Notes about transcription: occasional label mismatches (Speaker 2 -> Maya) and minor misheard acronyms (SAML transcribed as "sample" in a couple spots). The call had Q&A and a short recap and clear next steps.

End of transcript.
